ko.text: Production starts with all Must items
The line gets CE certification – without it, no production

name: E-bike Production Line
scope: Factory hall modifications, machine purchase and installation, certification, and software for production and maintenance.
intro: An e-bike maker is building a new production line. In 12 weeks the first bike should roll off it.
predWorld: Hall modifications, machine purchase and installation, CE certification. Long lead times and standards.
agileWorld: Production management software, a maintenance app and digital work instructions. Tuned with operators right on the line.

dependency.hint: Line machine integration is waiting for a predictive milestone: machine delivery.

workstreams.name: Production line installation
workstreams.why: Assembly and commissioning of machines follow a fixed technical plan with strict sequencing.

workstreams.name: Factory hall modifications
workstreams.why: Construction work with a permit and a clear specification. Changes are expensive.

workstreams.name: Machine safety certification (CE)
workstreams.why: The standards and certification process are set. They must be met completely and on time.

workstreams.name: Machine and spare parts procurement
workstreams.why: Tender and contracts with long lead times. The specification is clear up front.

workstreams.name: Manufacturing execution software (MES)
workstreams.why: Software can be built in parts and tuned based on experience from operations.

workstreams.name: Mobile app for maintenance staff
workstreams.why: Maintenance needs are best learned in practice – iterate directly with users.

workstreams.name: Digital work instructions
workstreams.why: Instructions improve based on feedback from operators right on the line.

workstreams.name: Experiment: predictive maintenance from sensor data
workstreams.why: Uncertain outcome – you need to experiment and learn from the data.

milestones.name: Machine delivery
milestones.okText: The machines arrived on time. They can be connected to the software from sprint 3.
milestones.lateText: Delivery was late. The machines can't be connected until sprint 4.

milestones.name: Installation and CE
milestones.okText: The line is installed and certified.
milestones.lateText: Installation ran late and certification slips. Management isn't thrilled.

milestones.name: Production start
milestones.okText: The first bike rolls off the line and operators report output in the new system!
milestones.lateText: Production is running, but key features are missing:

events.title: Machines stuck in customs
events.text: The machine shipment is stuck in customs. At least a two-week delay. The software team had planned the machine integration.
events.lesson: Dependencies between the predictive and agile parts belong in the risk register. The agile team can work around a delay (simulator, backlog replanning).

choices.text: Draw on the schedule buffer; meanwhile the software is developed against a machine simulator
choices.feedback: The simulator (a simple “digital twin”) caught bugs before the machines arrived.

choices.text: Pause the software team until the machines arrive
choices.feedback: The team waited two weeks, even though it could have worked on items with no dependency.

events.title: Operators don't want tablets
events.text: At the sprint review, operators declare: “The paper job sheets were faster.” They don't want to use the new system.
events.lesson: Managing change for people is part of the project. Involving users in iterations increases adoption.

choices.text: Involve the operators: testing on the line, changes based on their input and an “ambassador” on every shift
choices.feedback: After two iterations the system beats paper and operators recommend it to colleagues themselves.
Operators use the system, but enter data “blind” at the end of the shift.

choices.text: Run paper and the system side by side until the end of the project
choices.feedback: Double record-keeping is slow and the data drift apart.

events.title: Machine safety audit
events.text: The auditor finds that one station lacks an adequate safety guard. Without a fix, there's no CE certification.
events.lesson: Safety and certification are fixed requirements of the predictive part – never sacrificed for speed.

choices.text: Start change control, order the guard and adjust the installation schedule
choices.feedback: The guard arrived and certification passed. The delay fit within the buffer.

choices.text: Try to “talk your way” through certification
choices.feedback: The auditor didn't agree and company management is horrified.

choices.text: Remove the station from the line and run without it
choices.feedback: The line runs, but at lower capacity.

events.title: Customer wants an earlier start
events.text: A key customer wants the first bike delivery two weeks early. They're offering a higher price for it.
events.lesson: Fixed deadlines are negotiated through scope: delivering the most important part first (MVP) is a strength of hybrid.

choices.text: Analyze the impact and offer a limited start: Must software features and partial line capacity
choices.feedback: The customer got the first bikes early and the company a higher price. Full operation stayed on plan.

choices.text: Promise a full start two weeks early
choices.feedback: The customer is thrilled, both teams are in a panic.
The plan is protected, but the sales department is disappointed.

events.title: Machines on the office network?
events.text: IT security discovers the machines are supposed to be on the same network as the office computers. That's a security risk.
events.lesson: Cybersecurity concerns both parts: infrastructure is planned up front, software safeguards go into the Definition of Done.

choices.text: Add network segmentation to the installation plan and security to the Definition of Done
choices.feedback: The network is safely separated and every new feature passes a security check.

choices.text: Leave it – nobody's going to attack us
choices.feedback: A security risk now hangs over the whole production.

choices.text: Disconnect the machines from the network entirely
choices.feedback: Safe, but the software now gets no data from the machines.

events.title: The floor can't bear the press
events.text: The structural engineer finds the hall floor can't bear the new press. The foundations need reinforcing. The risk was in the register.
events.lesson: Identified risks should have a prepared response and a reserve. Well-separated project parts let the agile team keep going even when construction hits trouble.

choices.text: Activate the risk reserve and replan the installation; the software team carries on
choices.feedback: The response plan worked. Meanwhile, software development continues.
The engineer refused to sign off. You risk injuries and a fine.

choices.text: Stop the whole project until it's resolved
choices.feedback: The software has nothing to do with the floor. Time wasted for nothing.

choices.text: Negotiate emergency money with the sponsor and replan
choices.feedback: With no reserve ready, you have to find money and get a new plan approved. It costs time and trust.
